extends Node2D
## A fixture, not the game: Effect A over Level 1 at in-game camera scale, for
## the frame strip (CHANGE-BRIEF.md, section 6). Every capture of it is a
## fixture capture.
## The real level is the background, with its gameplay objects frozen; a
## frozen sprite of Rudy in CHAR-SWORD-SLASH, drawn as rudy.tscn draws him,
## stands at x = 2200 facing right, so his hitbox is at (2250, 764), where both
## bursts sit. Burst1 fires on frame 10; with `retrigger` on, Burst2 fires on
## frame 20, 0.333 s later at 30 fps, and Burst1 runs on. The two bursts are
## separate instances, as the overlap rule asks (A3), each with its own fixed
## seed, set in the scene. Frames are counted from 0, one per _process(), which
## is one Movie Maker frame. Capture at 30 fps with --quit-after 60.

const FIRST_FRAME := 10
const SECOND_FRAME := 20
## Level 1's gameplay objects, held still so the background does not change.
const FROZEN: Array[NodePath] = [^"Level1/Enemies", ^"Level1/Hazards", ^"Level1/SwordPickup",
	^"Level1/Waystone", ^"Level1/Portal"]

@export var retrigger := true

var _frame := 0


func _ready() -> void:
	for path in FROZEN:
		get_node(path).process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_DISABLED


func _process(_delta: float) -> void:
	if _frame == FIRST_FRAME:
		_fire($Burst1)
	elif _frame == SECOND_FRAME and retrigger:
		_fire($Burst2)
	_frame += 1


func _fire(burst: Node2D) -> void:
	for emitter: GPUParticles2D in burst.get_children():
		emitter.emitting = true
	print("PREVIEW frame %d: %s fired at %s" % [_frame, burst.name, burst.global_position])

## - this node's process_mode is ALWAYS (set in the scene). Its
##   _physics_process samples every physics tick, paused or not, and marks the
##   ticks on which the tree was paused, when nothing in the game ran;
## - it drives the scenarios with awaits on SceneTree's process_frame and
##   physics_frame signals, which the tree emits while paused;
## - Main is added under the tree's root, not under this node, so it inherits
##   the root's PAUSABLE mode as it does in the game. Under this node it would
##   inherit ALWAYS and never pause.
##
## Ticks. "st" counts from the tick a scenario's first key is read (st 0);
## setup ticks are negative. A swing tick counts the game ticks (ticks the tree
## was not paused) from the tick the press that starts the swing is read.
## At 30 fps a frame holds two ticks: slot a is the first, slot b the second. A
## key sent after a process_frame is read on the next frame's slot a. To have
## it read on slot b, the test awaits one physics_frame from a frame boundary,
## then sends the event and calls Input.flush_buffered_events() (the brief's
## second offset: one process_frame, then one physics_frame, then the event).
## Each swing's own press is read on slot a, so the edge presses read on slot
## a fall on its even swing ticks, and those on slot b on its odd ones.
##
## Prints a per-tick log, the scenarios, then the group EDGES, the ANOMALIES
## (the log lines around each failed check), and a RESULT line; quits 1 on any
## failure.

const MAIN_SCENE := preload("res://app/main.tscn")

const SETTLE_TICKS := 20 ## setup ticks after placing him, before the first key
## The slash (section 2.2, Revision 4): 17 ticks on screen, hitbox live on
## swing ticks 2-10, the swing over on tick 17.
const SWING_TICKS := 17
const LIVE_FIRST := 2

## A fresh press of `code` read on tick t: in slot a (the first tick of its
## frame, sent at the frame boundary) or, at two ticks a frame, in slot b
## (sent between the frame's two ticks and flushed). At one tick a frame the
## slot is ignored.
func _press(code: Key, t: int, slot: int) -> void:
	if _tpf == 1 or slot == 0:
		await _until(t)
		if _tick != t:
			_waits_failed.append("%s: a press for tick %d could only be sent for tick %d" % [_sc, t, _tick])
		_fresh(code, _tick)
		return
	await _until(t - 1)
	if _tick != t - 1:
		_waits_failed.append("%s: a slot-b press for tick %d: the frame boundary was at tick %d" % [_sc, t, _tick])
	await get_tree().physics_frame
	_fresh(code, t)
	Input.flush_buffered_events()


func _step(ticks: int) -> void:
	await _until(_tick + ticks)


## Steps whole frames until events sent next are read on tick t or later.
func _until(t: int) -> void:
#   Resource file not found   a missing ext_resource or typed load
#   Parse Error               a broken .tres/.tscn, or an ext_resource that
#                             names a missing file (the scene still loads)
#   Error loading resource    ResourceLoader.load() of a missing file
#   Failed to load script     a script that does not compile
#   couldn't resolve track    an animation track naming a node that does not
#                             exist (a WARNING; a missing property prints
#                             nothing, so the read-back test must check that)
# When one of these fails the run, the wrapper prints the lines it matched.
# Unchanged from the course: the realtime mode (no --fixed-fps, for tests that
# wait on audio), the optional timeout (120 s by default; status 124 means the
# test hung), the log name logs/<test>_<fps>fps.log or logs/<test>_realtime.log,
# and that exit code 0 does not mean no errors.
set -o pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 2
if [ $# -lt 2 ] || [ $# -gt 3 ] || [ ! -f "game/tests/$1" ]; then
	echo "usage: scripts/run-test.sh <test-file in game/tests/> <fps|realtime> [timeout-seconds]" >&2
	exit 2
fi
godot=${GODOT:-$(command -v godot || echo /Applications/Godot.app/Contents/MacOS/Godot)}
if [ "$2" = "realtime" ]; then
	fps_args=(); tag="realtime"
else
	fps_args=(--fixed-fps "$2"); tag="${2}fps"
fi
if [[ $1 == *.tscn ]]; then
	run_args=("res://tests/$1")
else
	run_args=(--script "res://tests/$1")
fi
mkdir -p logs
log="logs/$(basename "${1%.*}")_${tag}.log"
timeout "${3:-120}" "$godot" --headless "${fps_args[@]}" --path game "${run_args[@]}" 2>&1 | tee "$log"
status=$?
errors="SHADER ERROR|SCRIPT ERROR|Cannot open file|Failed loading resource|Resource file not found|Parse Error|Error loading resource|Failed to load script|couldn't resolve track"
if grep -qE "$errors" "$log"; then
	echo "run-test.sh: FAILED on an error line in $log:" >&2
	grep -nE "$errors" "$log" >&2
	status=1
fi
exit $status

class_name Rudy
extends CharacterBody2D
## Rudy's controller. It moves him and picks the clip that shows his state
## (_pick_clip); his Look plays that clip on its AnimationPlayer, which draws
## the pose's frame from the sheet. `pose` is the asset ID in
## CHARACTER-SHEET.md of the pose on screen. The origin is at his soles.
##
## In the air he shows the rising pose, and the falling pose only if he was
## moving sideways when the fall began. The falling pose leaps forward, so a
## jump straight up keeps the rising pose all the way down; the pose changes
## at most once in the air, at the top.
##
## On the ground, pressing the other direction turns him in place at once, with
## no slide; he moves that way only if the key is still held after
## turn_hold_time, so a tap turns him without moving him or the camera.
##
## Gear: the sword-and-shield pickup gives him the sword form, with its own
## poses (CHAR-SWORD-*). A fresh press of slash swings the sword once; its
## hitbox in front of him is live for part of the swing, and one cut defeats a
## goblin. No new swing starts until the last one ends.
##
## Damage (CHANGE-BRIEF.md): a hit knocks his gear away if he carries it, and
## otherwise costs one of his hearts. Either way it turns him toward the hit,
## knocks him back and makes him invulnerable for a moment, flashing; hits
## during that window are ignored. A fall below a cliff costs a heart too. At
## zero hearts he is defeated, and the level starts over from the opening, with
## his hearts full. He can only be hit by the collision capsule, so a hit that
## grazes his hair, his sword or his shield is a miss.
##
## The level also takes control away when he falls out of the level, while he
## gets back up after a respawn (always without gear), and while he celebrates
## on the teleport circle.
##
## The feel numbers are tuned by playtesting.

signal respawned ## he has got back up after a respawn, and control returns
signal hit ## a hit has just cost him his gear or a heart
signal hearts_changed(hearts: int)
signal defeated ## a hit took his last heart

enum Mode {
	WAITING, ## on the title, before play starts (CHAR-IDLE); no control
	PLAY, ## under the player's control
	HURT, ## knocked back by a hit (CHAR-HURT); no control for hurt_time
	DEFEATED, ## his last heart is gone (CHAR-DEFEAT); no control
	FALLEN, ## fell below a cliff; no control
	RESPAWNING, ## getting back up at a checkpoint (CHAR-RESPAWN); no control
	CELEBRATING, ## on the teleport circle (CHAR-CELEBRATE); no control
}

enum Gear { NONE, SWORD }

const ENEMY_LAYER := 4 ## the Enemy physics layer, for the sword's hitbox

@export_group("Feel")
@export var run_speed := 560.0 ## px/s
@export var run_accel := 5600.0 ## px/s²: full speed, or a stop, in 0.1 s
@export var turn_hold_time := 0.12 ## s the key is held after a turn on the ground before he moves
@export var gravity := 4000.0 ## px/s² on the way up
@export var fall_gravity := 6400.0 ## px/s² on the way down, so the fall is quicker than the rise
@export var jump_velocity := 1500.0 ## px/s; at 60 physics ticks/s the apex is 294 px, the rise takes 0.38 s and the fall 0.32 s
@export var respawn_time := 0.7 ## s in CHAR-RESPAWN before control returns
@export var stomp_bounce := 600.0 ## px/s upward after he lands on an enemy

@export_group("Sword")
@export var slash_time := 0.3 ## s a swing lasts (CHAR-SWORD-SLASH); no new swing until it ends
@export var slash_live_from := 0.03 ## s into the swing when the hitbox goes live
@export var slash_live_to := 0.18 ## s into the swing when it goes dead again
@export var slash_reach := 50.0 ## px from his centre to the centre of the hitbox, in front of him

@export_group("Damage")
@export var max_hearts := 3
@export var knockback := Vector2(350, 400) ## px/s: away from the hit, and up
@export var hurt_time := 0.35 ## s without control after a hit
@export var invulnerable_time := 1.2 ## s after a hit or a respawn in which hits are ignored
@export var flash_period := 0.12 ## s; he is see-through for half of each period while invulnerable

var facing := 1 ## 1 faces right, -1 faces left
## The asset ID of the pose on screen, read from the cell his Look's Sprite shows.
var pose: StringName:
	get:
		return _look.pose if _look else &"CHAR-IDLE"
var mode := Mode.PLAY ## the level sets WAITING while the title shows
var hearts := 3
var gear := Gear.NONE

var _turn_time_left := 0.0
var _respawn_time_left := 0.0
var _hurt_time_left := 0.0
var _invulnerable_left := 0.0
var _bounce_pending := false
var _was_falling := false
var _falls_sideways := false ## whether he was moving sideways when this fall began
var _slash_clock := -1.0 ## s into the current swing; below 0 when he is not swinging
var _slash_query := PhysicsShapeQueryParameters2D.new()

@onready var _look: RudyLook = $Look
@onready var _sword_box: CollisionShape2D = $SwordHitbox/Shape


func _ready() -> void:
	hearts = max_hearts
	_slash_query.shape = _sword_box.shape
	_slash_query.collision_mask = ENEMY_LAYER
	_slash_query.collide_with_areas = true
	_slash_query.collide_with_bodies = false
	# The player is never stopped when a state starts: it plays idle (cell 0,
	# the Sprite's frame before the first tick) from the start.
	_look.play_clip(&"idle")


## True while enemies and hazards can touch him: in play, or knocked back.
func can_be_touched() -> bool:
	return mode == Mode.PLAY or mode == Mode.HURT


func is_invulnerable() -> bool:
	return _invulnerable_left > 0.0


func is_slashing() -> bool:
	return _slash_clock >= 0.0


## The pickup gives him the sword and shield.
func equip_sword() -> void:
	gear = Gear.SWORD


## A hit from something at `from`. It knocks his gear away if he has any, and
## otherwise costs a heart, unless he cannot be touched or is still
## invulnerable; returns whether it did.
func take_hit(from: Vector2) -> bool:
	if not can_be_touched() or is_invulnerable():
		return false
	var away := signf(global_position.x - from.x)
	if away == 0.0:
		away = -facing
	var lost_gear := gear != Gear.NONE
	if lost_gear:
		_drop_gear(away)
	else:
		hearts -= 1
		hearts_changed.emit(hearts)
	Sfx.play(&"hurt")
	facing = -int(away) # he turns toward the hit
	_turn_time_left = 0.0
	_slash_clock = -1.0
	_invulnerable_left = invulnerable_time
	hit.emit()
	if not lost_gear and hearts <= 0:
		mode = Mode.DEFEATED
		velocity.x = 0.0
		defeated.emit()
	else:
		mode = Mode.HURT
		_hurt_time_left = hurt_time
		velocity = Vector2(away * knockback.x, -knockback.y)
	return true


## He landed on an enemy from above. The bounce starts on his next tick, so
## every enemy he lands on in the same tick sees him still falling.
func bounce() -> void:
	_bounce_pending = true


## He fell below a cliff: he keeps falling, out of the player's control, and
## the fall costs a heart (with no knockback; the level plays the hurt sound as
## he crosses the kill line). Returns whether it was his last heart.
func fall_out() -> bool:
	mode = Mode.FALLEN
	_slash_clock = -1.0
	hearts = maxi(hearts - 1, 0)
	hearts_changed.emit(hearts)
	return hearts == 0


## Puts him back on his feet at a checkpoint, without gear, facing right,
## getting back up, and invulnerable for a moment. After a defeat his hearts are
## full again; after a fall he keeps the ones he has left.
func respawn_at(spot: Vector2, refill_hearts: bool) -> void:
	global_position = spot
	velocity = Vector2.ZERO
	facing = 1
	gear = Gear.NONE
	_slash_clock = -1.0
	_turn_time_left = 0.0
	_bounce_pending = false
	if refill_hearts:
		hearts = max_hearts
		hearts_changed.emit(hearts)
	_invulnerable_left = invulnerable_time
	mode = Mode.RESPAWNING
	_respawn_time_left = respawn_time


func celebrate() -> void:
	mode = Mode.CELEBRATING
	_slash_clock = -1.0


func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
	if _bounce_pending:
		_bounce_pending = false
		velocity.y = -stomp_bounce
	var in_control := mode == Mode.PLAY
	var dir := _input_direction() if in_control else 0
	if dir != 0 and dir != facing:
		facing = dir
		if is_on_floor():
			velocity.x = 0.0
			_turn_time_left = turn_hold_time
	if dir == 0 or not is_on_floor():
		_turn_time_left = 0.0
	_turn_time_left = maxf(_turn_time_left - delta, 0.0)
	if not (mode == Mode.HURT and not is_on_floor()):
		# A knockback carries him until he lands; otherwise run, or slow down.
		var target_speed := 0.0 if _turn_time_left > 0.0 else dir * run_speed
		velocity.x = move_toward(velocity.x, target_speed, run_accel * delta)

	if not is_on_floor():
		velocity.y += (fall_gravity if velocity.y >= 0.0 else gravity) * delta
	elif in_control and Input.is_action_just_pressed(&"jump"):
		# A fresh press with ground underfoot: holding the key cannot jump again.
		velocity.y = -jump_velocity
		Sfx.play(&"jump")
	var new_swing := false
	if in_control and gear == Gear.SWORD and not is_slashing() and Input.is_action_just_pressed(&"slash"):
		# A fresh press, and not while a swing is under way: one sound per swing.
		_slash_clock = 0.0
		new_swing = true
		Sfx.play(&"slash")
	move_and_slide()

	_swing(delta)
	_count_down(delta)
	_look.scale.x = facing
	_look.modulate.a = 0.35 if is_invulnerable() and fmod(_invulnerable_left, flash_period) < flash_period / 2.0 else 1.0
	# Every new swing starts the slash clip over from its first key.
	_look.play_clip(_pick_clip(), new_swing)


## Moves the swing on and, while its hitbox is live, defeats every goblin in it.
## It asks the physics space directly, so the cut lands on the tick it reaches.
func _swing(delta: float) -> void:
	_sword_box.position.x = slash_reach * facing
	var live := is_slashing() and _slash_clock >= slash_live_from and _slash_clock <= slash_live_to
	_sword_box.disabled = not live
	if live:
		_slash_query.transform = _sword_box.global_transform
		for contact in get_world_2d().direct_space_state.intersect_shape(_slash_query, 8):
			if contact.collider is Goblin:
				(contact.collider as Goblin).defeat(&"slash")
	if is_slashing():
		_slash_clock += delta
		if _slash_clock >= slash_time:
			_slash_clock = -1.0


## The gear flies off, up and away from the hit, and fades.
func _drop_gear(away: float) -> void:
	gear = Gear.NONE
	var flying := FlyingGear.new()
	flying.position = global_position + Vector2(0, -80)
	flying.velocity = Vector2(away * 220.0, -420.0)
	get_parent().add_child(flying)


func _count_down(delta: float) -> void:
	_invulnerable_left = maxf(_invulnerable_left - delta, 0.0)
	if mode == Mode.HURT:
		_hurt_time_left -= delta
		if _hurt_time_left <= 0.0:
			mode = Mode.PLAY
	elif mode == Mode.RESPAWNING:
		_respawn_time_left -= delta
		if _respawn_time_left <= 0.0:
			mode = Mode.PLAY
			respawned.emit()


func _input_direction() -> int:
	var axis := Input.get_axis(&"move_left", &"move_right")
	if axis > 0.0:
		return 1
	if axis < 0.0:
		return -1
	return 0


## The clip for his state, by today's priorities (CHANGE-BRIEF.md section 3):
## higher in the list wins. Every name it returns is a StringName literal, so
## the read-back test can read them all from this file's text. The run's
## timing lives in the run clips' keys.
func _pick_clip() -> StringName:
	match mode:
		Mode.CELEBRATING:
			return &"celebrate"
		Mode.RESPAWNING:
			return &"respawn"
		Mode.DEFEATED:
			return &"defeat"
		Mode.HURT:
			return &"hurt"
	if is_slashing():
		return &"slash"
	var sword := gear == Gear.SWORD
	if not is_on_floor():
		var falling := velocity.y >= 0.0
		if falling and not _was_falling:
			_falls_sideways = absf(velocity.x) > 1.0
		_was_falling = falling
		if falling and _falls_sideways:
			return &"sword_fall" if sword else &"fall"
		return &"sword_rise" if sword else &"rise"
	_was_falling = false
	if absf(velocity.x) > 1.0:
		return &"sword_run" if sword else &"run"
	return &"sword_idle" if sword else &"idle"

## Rudy's generated frames (ASSET-LOG.md), one per pose asset ID in
## CHARACTER-SHEET.md, made by design/tools/matte_sprites.py into frames/.
## Every frame shares one canvas with the body origin (his soles, on the
## torso's centre line) at the same texture px, and is stored at 2 texture px
## per game px; the Sprite child draws it at half scale with that origin on
## this node's, as frames.json says. The controller flips this node to face
## left and fades it while he flashes. The Sprite's material adds the outer
## outline (systems/art/outline.gdshader), and it draws with mipmaps so the
## hair's fine lines do not shimmer at half scale.
## The sword form's frames show the sword and shield he holds, so nothing is
## drawn over them. CHAR-SWORD-BLOCK waits for blocking (build step 4).
##
## The Sprite draws the 16 frames from one sheet, sheet/rudy_sheet.png (4 x 4
## cells, in frames.json's order: CELLS). Its AnimationPlayer is the only
## writer of the Sprite's frame: this script plays the clip the controller
## picks and never sets the Sprite's texture or frame (CHANGE-BRIEF.md
## section 5). The pose on screen is read back from what is drawn: while the
## slash's cutout rig (SlashRig) shows, it is CHAR-SWORD-SLASH, the frame the
## rig is cut from; otherwise it is the pose of the cell the Sprite shows. The
## player is also the only writer of SlashRig's and the Sprite's visibility:
## this script only reads them (section 3).

const FRAMES: Dictionary[StringName, Texture2D] = {
	&"CHAR-IDLE": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-IDLE.png"),
	&"CHAR-RUN-A": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-RUN-A.png"),
	&"CHAR-RUN-B": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-RUN-B.png"),
	&"CHAR-RISE": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-RISE.png"),
	&"CHAR-FALL": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-FALL.png"),
	&"CHAR-HURT": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-HURT.png"),
	&"CHAR-DEFEAT": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-DEFEAT.png"),
	&"CHAR-RESPAWN": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-RESPAWN.png"),
	&"CHAR-CELEBRATE": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-CELEBRATE.png"),
	&"CHAR-SWORD-IDLE": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-SWORD-IDLE.png"),
	&"CHAR-SWORD-RUN-A": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-SWORD-RUN-A.png"),
	&"CHAR-SWORD-RUN-B": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-SWORD-RUN-B.png"),
	&"CHAR-SWORD-RISE": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-SWORD-RISE.png"),
	&"CHAR-SWORD-FALL": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-SWORD-FALL.png"),
	&"CHAR-SWORD-SLASH": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-SWORD-SLASH.png"),
	&"CHAR-SWORD-BLOCK": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-SWORD-BLOCK.png"),
}

## The sheet's cells, row by row: cell N shows the frame of CELLS[N]. This is
## frames.json's order (CHANGE-BRIEF.md section 2.1).
const CELLS: Array[StringName] = [
	&"CHAR-IDLE", &"CHAR-RUN-A", &"CHAR-RUN-B", &"CHAR-RISE",
	&"CHAR-FALL", &"CHAR-HURT", &"CHAR-DEFEAT", &"CHAR-RESPAWN",
	&"CHAR-CELEBRATE", &"CHAR-SWORD-IDLE", &"CHAR-SWORD-SLASH", &"CHAR-SWORD-BLOCK",
	&"CHAR-SWORD-RUN-A", &"CHAR-SWORD-RUN-B", &"CHAR-SWORD-RISE", &"CHAR-SWORD-FALL",
]

## The pose the slash rig draws: the frame its parts are cut from (section 2.2).
const RIG_POSE := &"CHAR-SWORD-SLASH"

## The asset ID of the pose on screen: RIG_POSE while SlashRig shows, else the
## pose of the cell the Sprite shows. It reads the nodes, not the clip asked
## for, and finds them by path, so it also reads true on a copy of Rudy that
## is not in the tree.
var pose: StringName:
	get:
		var rig := get_node_or_null(^"SlashRig") as CanvasItem
		if rig != null and rig.visible:
			return RIG_POSE
		var sprite := get_node_or_null(^"Sprite") as Sprite2D
		return CELLS[sprite.frame] if sprite else CELLS[0]

@onready var _player: AnimationPlayer = $AnimationPlayer


## Plays `clip` if it is not the clip playing. `restart` starts it over from
## its first key even if it is playing: every new swing does (section 3).
## The seek comes before play(): play() marks the clip as just started, so
## the player's update later this tick adds no time and shows the first key
## on this tick. A seek(0.0, true) after play() would run that update at once,
## using the mark up, and the tick's own update would then add a tick: the
## slash would end, and the player stop, a tick early.
func play_clip(clip: StringName, restart := false) -> void:
	if not restart and StringName(_player.current_animation) == clip:
		return
	if restart:
		_player.seek(0.0, true)
	_player.play(clip)


## The frame on screen now: the original PNG of the pose on screen. While the
## rig shows, that is CHAR-SWORD-SLASH.png, the frame the rig is cut from.
func frame() -> Texture2D:
	return FRAMES[pose]

## Rudy's controller. It moves him and picks the clip that shows his state
## (_pick_clip); his Look plays that clip on its AnimationPlayer, which draws
## the pose's frame from the sheet. `pose` is the asset ID in
## CHARACTER-SHEET.md of the pose on screen. The origin is at his soles.
##
## In the air he shows the rising pose, and the falling pose only if he was
## moving sideways when the fall began. The falling pose leaps forward, so a
## jump straight up keeps the rising pose all the way down; the pose changes
## at most once in the air, at the top.
##
## On the ground, pressing the other direction turns him in place at once, with
## no slide; he moves that way only if the key is still held after
## turn_hold_time, so a tap turns him without moving him or the camera.
##
## Gear: the sword-and-shield pickup gives him the sword form, with its own
## poses (CHAR-SWORD-*). A fresh press of slash swings the sword once; its
## hitbox in front of him is live for part of the swing, and one cut defeats a
## goblin. No new swing starts until the last one ends.
##
## Damage (CHANGE-BRIEF.md): a hit knocks his gear away if he carries it, and
## otherwise costs one of his hearts. Either way it turns him toward the hit,
## knocks him back and makes him invulnerable for a moment, flashing; hits
## during that window are ignored. A fall below a cliff costs a heart too. At
## zero hearts he is defeated, and the level starts over from the opening, with
## his hearts full. He can only be hit by the collision capsule, so a hit that
## grazes his hair, his sword or his shield is a miss.
##
## The level also takes control away when he falls out of the level, while he
## gets back up after a respawn (always without gear), and while he celebrates
## on the teleport circle.
##
## The feel numbers are tuned by playtesting.

## otherwise costs a heart, unless he cannot be touched or is still
## invulnerable; returns whether it did.
func take_hit(from: Vector2) -> bool:
	if not can_be_touched() or is_invulnerable():
		return false
	var away := signf(global_position.x - from.x)
	if away == 0.0:
		away = -facing
	var lost_gear := gear != Gear.NONE

	else:

	facing = -int(away) # he turns toward the hit
	_turn_time_left = 0.0
	_slash_clock = -1.0
	_invulnerable_left = invulnerable_time
	hit.emit()
	if not lost_gear and hearts <= 0:

	else:

	_bounce_pending = true

## the fall costs a heart (with no knockback; the level plays the hurt sound as
## he crosses the kill line). Returns whether it was his last heart.
func fall_out() -> bool:
	mode = Mode.FALLEN
	_slash_clock = -1.0

	hearts_changed.emit(hearts)

## Puts him back on his feet at a checkpoint, without gear, facing right,
## getting back up, and invulnerable for a moment. After a defeat his hearts are
## full again; after a fall he keeps the ones he has left.
func respawn_at(spot: Vector2, refill_hearts: bool) -> void:
	global_position = spot
	velocity = Vector2.ZERO
	facing = 1
	gear = Gear.NONE
	_slash_clock = -1.0
	_turn_time_left = 0.0
	_bounce_pending = false
	if refill_hearts:
		hearts = max_hearts
		hearts_changed.emit(hearts)

func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
	if _bounce_pending:
		_bounce_pending = false
		velocity.y = -stomp_bounce
	var in_control := mode == Mode.PLAY
	var dir := _input_direction() if in_control else 0
	if dir != 0 and dir != facing:
		facing = dir
		if is_on_floor():
			velocity.x = 0.0
			_turn_time_left = turn_hold_time
	if dir == 0 or not is_on_floor():
		_turn_time_left = 0.0
	_turn_time_left = maxf(_turn_time_left - delta, 0.0)
	if not (mode == Mode.HURT and not is_on_floor()):
		# A knockback carries him until he lands; otherwise run, or slow down.
		var target_speed := 0.0 if _turn_time_left > 0.0 else dir * run_speed
		velocity.x = move_toward(velocity.x, target_speed, run_accel * delta)

	if not is_on_floor():
		velocity.y += (fall_gravity if velocity.y >= 0.0 else gravity) * delta
	elif in_control and Input.is_action_just_pressed(&"jump"):
		# A fresh press with ground underfoot: holding the key cannot jump again.
		velocity.y = -jump_velocity
		Sfx.play(&"jump")
	var new_swing := false
	if in_control and gear == Gear.SWORD and not is_slashing() and Input.is_action_just_pressed(&"slash"):
		# A fresh press, and not while a swing is under way: one sound per swing.
		_slash_clock = 0.0
		new_swing = true
		Sfx.play(&"slash")
	move_and_slide()

	_swing(delta)
	_count_down(delta)
	_look.scale.x = facing
	_look.modulate.a = 0.35 if is_invulnerable() and fmod(_invulnerable_left, flash_period) < flash_period / 2.0 else 1.0
	# Every new swing starts the slash clip over from its first key.
	_look.play_clip(_pick_clip(), new_swing)


## Moves the swing on and, while its hitbox is live, defeats every goblin in it.
## It asks the physics space directly, so the cut lands on the tick it reaches.
func _swing(delta: float) -> void:
	_sword_box.position.x = slash_reach * facing
	var live := is_slashing() and _slash_clock >= slash_live_from and _slash_clock <= slash_live_to
	_sword_box.disabled = not live
	if live:
		_slash_query.transform = _sword_box.global_transform
		for contact in get_world_2d().direct_space_state.intersect_shape(_slash_query, 8):
			if contact.collider is Goblin:
				(contact.collider as Goblin).defeat(&"slash")
	if is_slashing():
		_slash_clock += delta
		if _slash_clock >= slash_time:
			_slash_clock = -1.0


## The gear flies off, up and away from the hit, and fades.
func _drop_gear(away: float) -> void:
	gear = Gear.NONE
	var flying := FlyingGear.new()
	flying.position = global_position + Vector2(0, -80)
	flying.velocity = Vector2(away * 220.0, -420.0)
	get_parent().add_child(flying)


func _count_down(delta: float) -> void:
	_invulnerable_left = maxf(_invulnerable_left - delta, 0.0)
	if mode == Mode.HURT:
		_hurt_time_left -= delta
		if _hurt_time_left <= 0.0:
			mode = Mode.PLAY
	elif mode == Mode.RESPAWNING:
		_respawn_time_left -= delta
		if _respawn_time_left <= 0.0:
			mode = Mode.PLAY
			respawned.emit()


func _input_direction() -> int:
	var axis := Input.get_axis(&"move_left", &"move_right")
	if axis > 0.0:
		return 1
	if axis < 0.0:

	return 0

## higher in the list wins. Every name it returns is a StringName literal, so
## the read-back test can read them all from this file's text. The run's
## timing lives in the run clips' keys.
func _pick_clip() -> StringName:
	match mode:
		Mode.CELEBRATING:
			return &"celebrate"
		Mode.RESPAWNING:
			return &"respawn"
		Mode.DEFEATED:
			return &"defeat"
		Mode.HURT:
			return &"hurt"
	if is_slashing():
		return &"slash"
	var sword := gear == Gear.SWORD
	if not is_on_floor():
		var falling := velocity.y >= 0.0
		if falling and not _was_falling:
			_falls_sideways = absf(velocity.x) > 1.0
		_was_falling = falling
		if falling and _falls_sideways:
			return &"sword_fall" if sword else &"fall"

	_was_falling = false

	return &"sword_idle" if sword else &"idle"

## CHARACTER-SHEET.md, made by design/tools/matte_sprites.py into frames/.
## Every frame shares one canvas with the body origin (his soles, on the
## torso's centre line) at the same texture px, and is stored at 2 texture px
## per game px; the Sprite child draws it at half scale with that origin on
## this node's, as frames.json says. The controller flips this node to face
## left and fades it while he flashes. The Sprite's material adds the outer
## outline (systems/art/outline.gdshader), and it draws with mipmaps so the
## hair's fine lines do not shimmer at half scale.
## The sword form's frames show the sword and shield he holds, so nothing is
## drawn over them. CHAR-SWORD-BLOCK waits for blocking (build step 4).
##
## The Sprite draws the 16 frames from one sheet, sheet/rudy_sheet.png (4 x 4
## cells, in frames.json's order: CELLS). Its AnimationPlayer is the only
## writer of the Sprite's frame: this script plays the clip the controller
## picks and never sets the Sprite's texture or frame (CHANGE-BRIEF.md
## section 5). The pose on screen is read back from what is drawn: while the
## slash's cutout rig (SlashRig) shows, it is CHAR-SWORD-SLASH, the frame the
## rig is cut from; otherwise it is the pose of the cell the Sprite shows. The
## player is also the only writer of SlashRig's and the Sprite's visibility:
## this script only reads them (section 3).

const FRAMES: Dictionary[StringName, Texture2D] = {
	&"CHAR-IDLE": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-IDLE.png"),
	&"CHAR-RUN-A": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-RUN-A.png"),

	&"CHAR-HURT": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-HURT.png"),

	&"CHAR-RESPAWN": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-RESPAWN.png"),
	&"CHAR-CELEBRATE": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-CELEBRATE.png"),
	&"CHAR-SWORD-IDLE": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-SWORD-IDLE.png"),
	&"CHAR-SWORD-RUN-A": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-SWORD-RUN-A.png"),
	&"CHAR-SWORD-RUN-B": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-SWORD-RUN-B.png"),
	&"CHAR-SWORD-RISE": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-SWORD-RISE.png"),
	&"CHAR-SWORD-FALL": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-SWORD-FALL.png"),
	&"CHAR-SWORD-SLASH": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-SWORD-SLASH.png"),
	&"CHAR-SWORD-BLOCK": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-SWORD-BLOCK.png"),
}

## The sheet's cells, row by row: cell N shows the frame of CELLS[N]. This is
## frames.json's order (CHANGE-BRIEF.md section 2.1).
const CELLS: Array[StringName] = [
	&"CHAR-IDLE", &"CHAR-RUN-A", &"CHAR-RUN-B", &"CHAR-RISE",
	&"CHAR-FALL", &"CHAR-HURT", &"CHAR-DEFEAT", &"CHAR-RESPAWN",
	&"CHAR-CELEBRATE", &"CHAR-SWORD-IDLE", &"CHAR-SWORD-SLASH", &"CHAR-SWORD-BLOCK",
	&"CHAR-SWORD-RUN-A", &"CHAR-SWORD-RUN-B", &"CHAR-SWORD-RISE", &"CHAR-SWORD-FALL",
]

## The pose the slash rig draws: the frame its parts are cut from (section 2.2).
const RIG_POSE := &"CHAR-SWORD-SLASH"

## The asset ID of the pose on screen: RIG_POSE while SlashRig shows, else the
## pose of the cell the Sprite shows. It reads the nodes, not the clip asked
## for, and finds them by path, so it also reads true on a copy of Rudy that
## is not in the tree.
var pose: StringName:
	get:
		var rig := get_node_or_null(^"SlashRig") as CanvasItem
		if rig != null and rig.visible:
			return RIG_POSE
		var sprite := get_node_or_null(^"Sprite") as Sprite2D
		return CELLS[sprite.frame] if sprite else CELLS[0]

@onready var _player: AnimationPlayer = $AnimationPlayer


## Plays `clip` if it is not the clip playing. `restart` starts it over from
## its first key even if it is playing: every new swing does (section 3).
## The seek comes before play(): play() marks the clip as just started, so
## the player's update later this tick adds no time and shows the first key
## on this tick. A seek(0.0, true) after play() would run that update at once,
## using the mark up, and the tick's own update would then add a tick: the
## slash would end, and the player stop, a tick early.
func play_clip(clip: StringName, restart := false) -> void:
	if not restart and StringName(_player.current_animation) == clip:
		return
	if restart:
		_player.seek(0.0, true)
	_player.play(clip)


## The frame on screen now: the original PNG of the pose on screen. While the
## rig shows, that is CHAR-SWORD-SLASH.png, the frame the rig is cut from.
func frame() -> Texture2D:
	return FRAMES[pose]

extends Node2D
## A fixture, not the game: Rudy's slash over Level 1 at in-game camera scale,
## for the slash frame strip (CHANGE-BRIEF.md, Revision 5, "The frame strip";
## section 4, "The rendered frame"; section 9, "Frame strips and watching").
## Every capture of it is a fixture capture.
##
## The real level is the background, with its Enemies, Hazards, Waystone and
## Portal frozen (PROCESS_MODE_DISABLED); its SwordPickup is left alone. The
## real Rudy (content/rudy/rudy.tscn) stands at (2500, 840), on the pickup, so
## he takes the sword by touch on the first ticks, facing right. He is driven
## only by Input.parse_input_event key events: this script never writes his
## state, velocity, position, gear or his AnimationPlayer, and only reads them.
## The camera has Main's limits, y 540 and no smoothing, and its x is set to
## Rudy's x every frame, so his origin stays at one screen point.
##
## J is read on tick 60, the first tick of frame 30 at 30 fps, and again every
## 120 ticks after it, so a 90-frame capture holds one swing and a windowed run
## without Movie Maker shows a swing every 2 s. With the user argument
## second-tick, each J is read one tick later, on the second tick of its frame
## (the brief's second offset, section 6), sent as the edge test sends a slot-b
## press (tests/test_rudy_edges.gd): after the frame boundary, one physics_frame,
## then the event and Input.flush_buffered_events().
##
## Ticks are counted from 0, from this node's _physics_process, which runs
## before Rudy's on each tick; frames are counted from 0, one per _process(),
## which is one Movie Maker frame. Each frame prints one line, "frame N", with
## the ticks run in it and the state after its last tick; a header before
## frame 0 names the frames to read.
##
## Run from the assignment folder. Windowed:
##   godot --path game res://previews/slash_preview.tscn
##   godot --path game res://previews/slash_preview.tscn -- second-tick
## Capture (the assignment text's command, with --debug-collisions; r<N> is the
## take; the second offset adds "-- second-tick" at the end):
##   godot --path game res://previews/slash_preview.tscn \
##     --write-movie "$PWD/captures/slash/r<N>/frame.png" \
##     --fixed-fps 30 --quit-after 90 --debug-collisions \
##     2>&1 | tee logs/slash_preview_r<N>.log

const FIRST_READ_TICK := 60 ## the first J is read on this tick (slot a)
const REPEAT_TICKS := 120
const TRIGGER_FRAME := 30 ## at 30 fps, frame 30 holds ticks 60 and 61
## Level 1's gameplay objects, held still so the background does not change.
const FROZEN: Array[NodePath] = [^"Level1/Enemies", ^"Level1/Hazards",
	^"Level1/Waystone", ^"Level1/Portal"]
const ARGUMENTS := ["second-tick"]

var _second_tick := false
var _tick := 0 ## the number of ticks started so far: the next tick's number
var _frame := 0
var _frame_first_tick := 0 ## the first tick of the frame now running
var _next_send := FIRST_READ_TICK ## the next J is sent for the first tick >= this
var _j_down := false
var _was_slashing := false
var _swing_start := -1 ## the tick the current swing's J was read on

@onready var _rudy: Rudy = $Rudy
@onready var _player: AnimationPlayer = $Rudy/Look/AnimationPlayer
@onready var _sprite: Sprite2D = $Rudy/Look/Sprite
@onready var _rig: Node2D = $Rudy/Look/SlashRig
@onready var _lean: Node2D = $Rudy/Look/SlashRig/Lean
@onready var _grip: Node2D = $Rudy/Look/SlashRig/Lean/Grip
@onready var _arc: Sprite2D = $Rudy/Look/SlashRig/Lean/Arc
@onready var _hitbox: CollisionShape2D = $Rudy/SwordHitbox/Shape
@onready var _camera: Camera2D = $Camera
@onready var _label: Label = $Overlay/Label


func _ready() -> void:
	var args := OS.get_cmdline_user_args()
	for arg in args:
		if not arg in ARGUMENTS:
			print("# slash_preview: unknown argument %s; known: %s" % [arg, ", ".join(ARGUMENTS)])
			get_tree().quit(1)
			return
	_second_tick = "second-tick" in args
	for path in FROZEN:
		get_node(path).process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_DISABLED
	_print_header()


func _physics_process(_delta: float) -> void:
	_observe(_tick - 1) # Rudy has not run this tick yet: the state after the last one
	_tick += 1


func _process(_delta: float) -> void:
	_observe(_tick - 1)
	_camera.position.x = _rudy.global_position.x
	_camera.force_update_scroll()
	_label.text = "FIXTURE slash_preview frame %d" % _frame
	print(_line())
	_frame += 1
	_frame_first_tick = _tick
	_drive()


## Sends this frame boundary's key events, read on the next tick (slot a), or
## on the one after it (slot b, the second offset).
func _drive() -> void:
	if _j_down:
		_key(KEY_J, false)
	if _tick >= _next_send:
		_next_send += REPEAT_TICKS
		if _second_tick:
			await get_tree().physics_frame
			_key(KEY_J, true)
			Input.flush_buffered_events()
		else:
			_key(KEY_J, true)


func _key(code: Key, pressed: bool) -> void:
	var e := InputEventKey.new()
	e.physical_keycode = code
	e.pressed = pressed
	Input.parse_input_event(e)
	if code == KEY_J:
		_j_down = pressed


## Notes the tick a swing starts on, from Rudy's state after tick `done`.
func _observe(done: int) -> void:
	var slashing := _rudy.is_slashing()
	if slashing and not _was_slashing:
		_swing_start = done
	_was_slashing = slashing


func _line() -> String:
	var ticks := "%3d-%3d" % [_frame_first_tick, _tick - 1] if _tick > _frame_first_tick else "   none"
	var swing := "%2d" % (_tick - 1 - _swing_start) if _rudy.is_slashing() else " -"
	var v := _rudy.velocity
	var lp := _lean.position
	var o := _rudy.get_global_transform_with_canvas().origin
	return ("frame %3d ticks %s mode %-11s pose %-16s gear %-5s facing %+d x %8.2f y %7.2f"
		+ " vel (%8.2f, %8.2f) floor %-5s clip %-10s pos %.4f cell %2d sprite %-5s rig %-5s"
		+ " grip %7.2f lean %6.2f lean_pos (%5.2f, %5.2f) arc %.3f live %-5s swing %s"
		+ " screen (%7.2f, %7.2f)") % [
		_frame, ticks, Rudy.Mode.keys()[_rudy.mode], _rudy.pose, Rudy.Gear.keys()[_rudy.gear],
		_rudy.facing, _rudy.global_position.x, _rudy.global_position.y, v.x, v.y,
		_rudy.is_on_floor(), _player.current_animation, _player.current_animation_position,
		_sprite.frame, _sprite.visible, _rig.visible, _grip.rotation_degrees,
		_lean.rotation_degrees, lp.x, lp.y, _arc.modulate.a, not _hitbox.disabled, swing, o.x, o.y]


func _print_header() -> void:
	var f := TRIGGER_FRAME
	print("# FIXTURE slash_preview: a fixture, not the game; every capture of it is a fixture capture")
	print("# argument: %s" % ("second-tick (J read on the second tick of its frame)" if _second_tick
		else "none (J read on the first tick of its frame)"))
	print("# J read on tick %d, then every %d ticks; at 30 fps frame N runs ticks 2N and 2N+1 and shows the state after 2N+1"
		% [FIRST_READ_TICK + (1 if _second_tick else 0), REPEAT_TICKS])
	print("# trigger frame F = %d" % f)
	print("# frames to read:")
	if not _second_tick:
		print("#   (CHANGE-BRIEF.md, Revision 5, \"The frame strip\")")
		print("#   F-1 = %d  before the press: the sword-idle Sprite" % (f - 1))
		print("#   F   = %d  tick 1, startup: the rig: blade raised back over his shoulder, Grip -67.5, Lean -2; no arc; hitbox dead" % f)
		print("#   F+1 = %d  tick 3, active, the first frame shown: blade starting forward, Grip -53.3; arc half on (a 0.5); hitbox live" % (f + 1))
		print("#   F+2 = %d  tick 5, active: blade at its drawn angle (0); Lean +3, 6 px forward; arc a 0.86" % (f + 2))
		print("#   F+3 = %d  tick 7, active: blade at +5: almost where F+2 left it, the stall of Revision 4" % (f + 3))
		print("#   F+5 = %d  tick 11, recovery, the first frame: blade forward and down at +45; arc gone; hitbox dead" % (f + 5))
		print("#   F+8 = %d  tick 17, the swing is over: the sword-idle Sprite again" % (f + 8))
		print("#   tick 2, the startup-to-active boundary, falls on the first tick of frame F+1: no PNG shows it")
	else:
		print("#   DERIVED, not the brief's: the brief has no table for this offset. Derived from the phase table")
		print("#   (section 2.2: startup 0-1, active 2-10, recovery 11-16, end 17) and the slash clip's keys and")
		print("#   transitions (Grip ease 2 into tick 11, 0.5 from it; Lean ease 0.5 from tick 11; Arc linear).")
		print("#   Frame N shows swing tick 2N - 60.")
		print("#   F-1 = %d  before the press: the sword-idle Sprite" % (f - 1))
		print("#   F   = %d  tick 0, startup, the trigger: the rig; Grip -70, Lean -2, Lean (0, 0); arc a 0; hitbox dead" % f)
		print("#   F+1 = %d  tick 2, the startup-to-active boundary, the first active key: Grip -60, Lean -2, Lean (0, 0); arc a 0; hitbox live" % (f + 1))
		print("#   F+2 = %d  tick 4, active: Grip -33.33, Lean +1.33, Lean (4, 0); arc a 1.0; hitbox live" % (f + 2))
		print("#   F+5 = %d  tick 10, the last live tick: Grip +31.25, Lean +3, Lean (6, 0); arc a 0.14; hitbox live" % (f + 5))
		print("#   F+6 = %d  tick 12, recovery, the first frame shown: Grip +35.83, Lean +2.08, Lean (4.17, 0); arc a 0; hitbox dead" % (f + 6))
		print("#   F+8 = %d  tick 16, the last slash frame: Grip +15.83, Lean +0.08, Lean (0.17, 0); arc a 0; hitbox dead" % (f + 8))
		print("#   F+9 = %d  tick 18, the first frame after the swing: the sword-idle Sprite again" % (f + 9))
		print("#   ticks 11 (active-to-recovery) and 17 (the end) fall on the first ticks of frames F+6 and F+9: no PNG shows them")
	print("# columns: the ticks run in the frame, then the state after its last tick; swing = ticks since the J was read")

- `godot --headless --path game --fixed-fps 30 --quit-after 90 res://previews/slash_preview.tscn 2>&1 | tee logs/slash_preview_headless.log`, with and without extra commands around it.

```bash
godot --headless --path game --fixed-fps 30 --quit-after 90 res://previews/slash_preview.tscn 2>&1 | tee logs/slash_preview_headless.log
godot --headless --path game --fixed-fps 30 --quit-after 90 res://previews/slash_preview.tscn -- second-tick 2>&1 | tee logs/slash_preview_headless_second_tick.log
godot --headless --path game --fixed-fps 30 --quit-after 90 res://previews/run_preview.tscn 2>&1 | tee logs/run_preview_headless.log
godot --headless --path game --fixed-fps 30 --quit-after 90 res://previews/run_preview.tscn -- sword 2>&1 | tee logs/run_preview_headless_sword.log

**The `res://` path count will probably be 102, not 100.** `checks.gd`'s `_res_paths_named_in` counts every `res://` string in `.gd` and `.tscn` files, comments included. Today's count is 98 (`logs/checks_60fps.log:143`). Four paths are new:
- the two scripts, named in the new `.tscn` files;
- the two scenes, named in the run and capture commands in each script's header comment.

All four exist, so the check should still pass. It just won't read 100. I kept the text's command with its `res://` path in the headers. If you want 100, those comment lines would have to drop the `res://` prefix.

**What the scripts do**
- **Input.** Rudy is the real `rudy.tscn` at (2500, 840). He gets only `parse_input_event` key events; the scripts only read his state.
- **When the keys are read.**
  - In `slash_preview`, J is read on tick 60 and every 120 ticks after.
  - With `-- second-tick`, it waits one `physics_frame` past the frame boundary, then sends J and calls `Input.flush_buffered_events()`, as `test_rudy_edges.gd` does. J should then be read on tick 61.
  - In `run_preview`, D is read on tick 60 and released on tick 84. With no argument, the SwordPickup is disabled and hidden in `_ready`. With `-- sword` it is left alone.
- **Swing tick.** The log doesn't assume the planned tick. It records the tick on which `is_slashing()` first comes back true, and counts the swing from there.
- **Log.** Each rendered frame prints one `frame N` line with fixed decimals, and the corner label shows the frame number. The camera is updated with `force_update_scroll()` before the screen origin is read, so the origin isn't a frame behind.
- **The second offset's table is derived, not the brief's.** It is computed from the slash track's keys and easing, and it says so in its header:

  | Frame | Swing tick | Grip | Lean | Lean x | Arc α | Hitbox |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | F−1 = 29 | before the press | sword-idle Sprite | | | | |
  | F = 30 | 0 | −70 | −2 | 0 | 0 | dead |
  | F+1 = 31 | 2 | −60 | −2 | 0 | 0 | live |
  | F+2 = 32 | 4 | −33.33 | +1.33 | 4 | 1 | live |
  | F+5 = 35 | 10 | +31.25 | +3 | 6 | 0.14 | live |
  | F+6 = 36 | 12 | +35.83 | +2.08 | 4.17 | 0 | dead |
  | F+8 = 38 | 16 | +15.83 | +0.08 | 0.17 | 0 | dead |
  | F+9 = 39 | 18 | sword-idle Sprite | | | | |

  Revision 5's own values for ticks 1, 3, 5 and 7 (−67.5, −53.3, 0, +5) agree with the same keys.
- **Run frames to read.** The header lists frames 30–41 and derives the expected cells: frames 30–33 A, 34–36 B, 37–40 A, 41 B.

**Not yet checked, because nothing ran**
- That frame 0 holds ticks 0–1.
- That the slot-b press really lands on tick 61.
- That the disabled pickup stays untaken in the no-argument run.
- That the screen origin holds at one point.

The logs above would show each of these.
